LEADERSHIP + AI / NIMISHA SUREKA

Making leadership learning stick

How I used AI to build a tool that helps managers revisit leadership lessons and turn reflection into a practical plan.

October 27, 20262 min read

I work in HR. I’ve never formally studied coding. And I built a website to help our people managers put leadership learning into practice.

After a leadership development session, we often hear a fair question: How do we help people retain what they learned and use it when a real challenge comes up?

It’s a question I’ve asked myself, too. A workshop can create a powerful moment of reflection, but the real test comes later: in a difficult conversation, a team misunderstanding, or a decision a manager needs to make.

I wanted our managers to have a way to revisit what they learned in our Self-Aware Leader and Insights sessions, reflect on the situation in front of them, and build a practical plan for what to try next.

So I built one.

With ChatGPT and Codex Sites, I created a working website for my organization without a coding background or technical support. Along the way, I found myself playing several roles: consultant, designer, builder, and even salesperson when it came time to explain why the tool could help.

As someone from HR who once would have assumed that building a website was outside my reach, that has been exhilarating.

The part I’m most excited about is what the tool makes possible for managers. Leadership learning matters when it shapes how we listen, work through differences, and support our teams. AI gave me a way to turn an idea for helping with that into something people can actually use.

It has also changed how I think about my own role. When we see an organizational need, we may now be able to do more than propose a solution. We can start building one.
